# Disagreement Log — Acts of Thomas, Chapter 1
**Agents:** EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 12

---

## Verse-by-Verse Disagreements

### v.1 — "cast lots" vs. "divided... by lot"
- **EMET:** "we divided up the regions... by lot"
- **LOGOS:** "divided the regions... allotted by lot"
- **PNEUMA:** "We cast lots to divide the world"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's active "cast lots" is a vivid rendering; "allotted by lot" (LOGOS) is redundant; EMET is more straightforward.

### v.3 — "I do not have the strength" vs. "I have no strength for this"
- **EMET:** "I do not have the strength to go, for I am weak in body"
- **LOGOS:** "I have no strength for this journey, for I am weak in body"
- **PNEUMA:** "I don't have the strength. I'm not well."
- **Note:** PNEUMA drops "weak in body" and substitutes "I'm not well" — a paraphrase that loses the specific physical/bodily dimension of the Syriac.

### v.3 — "Hebrew man" vs. "a Hebrew"
- **EMET:** "I — a Hebrew man — go among the Indians"
- **LOGOS:** "I — a Hebrew — go among the Indians"
- **PNEUMA:** "I am a Hebrew"
- **Note:** All acceptable. EMET's "Hebrew man" is slightly more literal; the "man" adds ethnic specificity.

### v.4 — "by night" vs. "at night"
- **EMET:** "appeared to him in a vision by night"
- **LOGOS:** "appeared to him at night in a vision"
- **Note:** Minor preposition placement.

### v.5 — "Send me wherever you wish" vs. "Send me wherever you will" vs. "Send me anywhere you want"
- **EMET:** "wherever you wish"
- **LOGOS:** "wherever you will"
- **PNEUMA:** "anywhere you want"
- **Note:** Register disagreement. "Wherever you will" (LOGOS) preserves the formal address; "anywhere you want" (PNEUMA) is colloquial.

### v.6 — "a certain merchant from India was there" vs. "happened to be in the city"
- **EMET:** "a certain merchant from India was there"
- **LOGOS:** "was present"
- **PNEUMA:** "happened to be in the city"
- **Note:** "Happened to be" (PNEUMA) implies coincidence; the theological point is that nothing here is coincidental. "Was present" (LOGOS) is neutral.

### v.7 — "Do you wish to buy a carpenter?" vs. "Are you looking to buy a carpenter?"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "Do you wish to buy a carpenter?"
- **PNEUMA:** "Are you looking to buy a carpenter?"
- **Note:** Minor register difference. "Do you wish" is more formal.

### v.10 — Bill of sale rendering
- All agents agree on the content. PNEUMA uses a more colloquial frame ("The document read:"). EMET/LOGOS use "The writing ran thus:"
- **Note:** SOPHIA prefers LOGOS's "The writing ran thus" for its legal-document formality.

### v.10 — "declares" vs. "hereby declare" vs. "hereby sell"
- **EMET:** "declare that I have sold"
- **LOGOS:** "hereby declare that I have sold"
- **PNEUMA:** "hereby sell"
- **Note:** "Hereby sell" (PNEUMA) drops the declarative framing of the legal document. LOGOS's full form is preferred.

### v.12 — "Is this your master?" vs. "Is this man your master?"
- **EMET:** "Is this your master?"
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "Is this man your master?"
- **Note:** The addition of "man" (LOGOS) clarifies the referent. Minor.

### v.13 — "Yes, he is my Lord" — all agents agree.

### v.14 — "held his peace" vs. "was silent" vs. "said nothing"
- **EMET:** "held his peace"
- **LOGOS:** "was silent"
- **PNEUMA:** "said nothing"
- **Note:** "Held his peace" (EMET) is archaic but powerful; "was silent" (LOGOS) is neutral; "said nothing" (PNEUMA) is colloquial. SOPHIA prefers "was silent" for its combination of readability and weight.

---
*12 disagreements. SOPHIA: "was silent" (v.14); formal "Do you wish" (v.7); retain "weak in body" (v.3); bill of sale in legal formality (v.10).*
